paragraphs: The ML350 has been part of the M-Class range since 1997. Early W163-generation cars use the M112 — a 3.2-litre V6 petrol. From 2005, the W164-generation ML350 uses the M272, a 3.5-litre V6 petrol. The full breakdown by engine code is below.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every ML350 on the road.

cards.body: A 3.2-litre V6 petrol engine fitted to the ML350 from 1997 to 2005 in the W163 generation. No specific known issue has been independently confirmed for this application. We replace timing chains, bearings and gaskets as standard on every rebuild.

A 3.5-litre V6 petrol engine fitted to the ML350 from 2005 to 2011 in the W164 generation. No specific known issue has been independently confirmed for this application. We service it to the same standard as our other ML350 rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the ML350 spans two distinct V6 engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M112 part will work on an M272 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic M-Class quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
